materialReview.scope: Native combat camera visual review of the configured Lichenfang palette.
materialReview.result: The dark spruce, slate, teal lichen, copper leaf accents, and amber eye palette are visibly distinct in the captured combat view. This is not a lighting sweep, shader-channel inspection, or final art-direction approval.

selectedPNGs.observation: The complete authored lichen-armored wolf renders together in the native combat camera with a readable head, layered mane, legs, tail, and leaf accents.
A later idle sample retains the same connected silhouette; no detached authored piece is visible.
The exact enemy AttackProf trigger is recorded at this sample; the visible body remains coherent as the native controller begins its attack transition.
Native attack motion bends the bound creature forward while its legs, mane, tail, and lichen layers remain visibly joined.
Later attack follow-through remains a readable wolf-like silhouette despite the native combat camera and effects.
The exact ordinary player damage trigger is recorded at this sample; the model stays visible through the initial native hit effect.
The nonlethal damaged pose deforms the same full authored body without a lost renderer or detached limb.
The end of the damaged response remains connected and visually legible before the later native enemy turn.
The separate explicit fixture records the exact native Death trigger while the bound creature is still visible.
The deathHeavy_wolf clip moves the full lichen-armored body into its native death pose without an obvious renderer loss.
A later death clip sample shows the creature lying in a coherent defeated pose before the victory UI; this is not a ragdoll finding.

limits: This review covers the exact enbaseywolf / wolfA / Wolfie source pair only; direct wolfA and other wolf-family resource prefabs require their own trials.
The native camera, foreground hero, and combat effects sometimes obscure close surface detail.
The ordinary hit is nonlethal; the separate explicit KillSingle transition is not ordinary lethal-damage acceptance.
The native death clip remains animator-driven and no rigidbodies were recorded, so this is not a ragdoll or settled-corpse review.
Culling envelope, portraits, long-session resource lifetime, other native ability variants, and final art-direction approval remain separate work.
